params.body:
Two methods on `IDbRepository` carry a required parameter behind one that has a default.

```php
public function wherein($fields = ['*'], $key, $value = [], ...);
public function paginate($fields = ['*'], $params = [], $with = [], $order = null, $paginate = 20, $request);
```

PHP treats `$key` and `$request` as required anyway, and says so: **twenty deprecation notices every
time these two files are loaded**, in the log of every environment, on main today. In PHP 9 that is
an error rather than a notice.

The order stays exactly as every caller knows it — the trailing parameters simply carry a default of
their own now, in the interface and in the implementation. Zero notices after.

**And while in there, the contract was lying twice.** The interface declared `get()` with five
required parameters while `DbRepository::get()` gives `$with_trashed` a default, and `update()` with
two while the implementation takes three. By the contract, seventy-five calls in this codebase were
wrong. Nobody noticed, because PHP checks a call against the concrete class and not against the
interface — but anyone implementing `IDbRepository` fresh would have been forced to require all
five, and would have had no way to know that was a mistake rather than the design.

Baseline 1.617 → 1.600, 17 entries gone, none added. 1.826 tests green.

params.title: Two signatures that PHP has been complaining about twenty times a load
